title: An immediate prime-degree extension forces an unattained polynomial infimum
statement: All fields below are fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. For such a field $A$, write $A^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ for its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde A=A^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_A=|A^\times|$. For a finite extension $B/A$ set $e(B/A)=[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]$, $f(B/A)=[\widetilde B:\widetilde A]$ and $d(B/A)=[B:A]/(e(B/A)f(B/A))$. Call it immediate if its value group and residue field equal those of $A$, unramified if $e=d=1$ and the residue extension is separable, and tame if $d=1$, its residue extension is separable and its ramification index is prime to the residue characteristic (with no index restriction in residue characteristic zero). A field extension is separable if every algebraic element has a minimal polynomial with distinct roots. Let $A$ be complete with $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde A)>0$ and let $B/A$ be immediate of degree $p$. There exist $a,b\in A$ with $s=\inf_{c\in A}|c^p-ac+b|>0$, $|pb|<s$, and $|c^p-ac+b|>s$ for every $c\in A$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.1, p. 36; reformulated and proved as Proposition 6.1.4(i),(iv)(a), pp. 38–40. No discreteness or separability of B/A assumed.

proof.text: Choose $\alpha\in B\setminus A$. The residue characteristic $p$ is prime, hence $p\ge2$. Degree multiplicativity gives $[A(\alpha):A]>1$ dividing $[B:A]=p$, so $A(\alpha)=B$. Let $f\in A[T]$ be its monic minimal polynomial. Its degree is $p$: the kernel description of the minimal polynomial identifies $A[\alpha]$ with $A[T]/(f)$, whose basis is $1,T,\ldots,T^{\deg f-1}$ by monic division; $A[\alpha]$ is a field because it is a finite-dimensional domain over $A$, so it equals $A(\alpha)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, immediate cases, printed p. 39: choose a non-base-field element and its degree-p monic minimal polynomial.

proof.text: For any $x\in B\setminus A$, put $r_x=\inf_{c\in A}|x-c|$. It is positive: if it were zero, choose $c_n\in A$ with $|x-c_n|<1/n$; this is Cauchy, and its limit in the complete field $A$ would equal $x$. No distance is minimal. Indeed, for $y=x-c\ne0$, equality of value groups gives $t\in A^\times$ with $|t|=|y|$, and equality of residue fields gives $u\in A^\circ$ with the same residue as $y/t$. Thus $|y/t-u|<1$ and $|x-(c+tu)|<|x-c|$. Consequently $r_x<|x-c|$ for every $c\in A$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, immediate case, printed p. 39: positivity by completeness and nonattainment by immediacy, with both arguments expanded.

proof.text: For $c\in A$, the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha-c$ is $f(T+c)$: substitution is an invertible automorphism of $A[T]$ preserving monicity, irreducibility and degree, and the polynomial vanishes at $\alpha-c$. The constant-term norm formula therefore gives $$|f(c)|=|\alpha-c|^p.$$ This argument applies to any non-base-field generator of $B/A$, with its own monic minimal polynomial. In particular its constant term has norm equal to the $p$th power of the norm of that generator.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed pp. 39–40: constant-term and evaluation norms; use the general Mathlib formula instead of introducing a second root and applying Krasner.

proof.text: First suppose $f$ is inseparable. Since $f$ is irreducible, failure of coprimality with its derivative forces $f\mid f\prime$; as $\deg f\prime<p$, it follows that $f\prime=0$. Coefficientwise differentiation then forces the characteristic of $A$ to be $p$ and every coefficient of degrees $1,\ldots,p-1$ to vanish: the leading derivative coefficient is $p$, and each of $1,\ldots,p-1$ is nonzero in characteristic $p$. Thus $f(T)=T^p+b$. Take $a=0$ and $r=r_\alpha$. The preceding two steps give $\inf_c|c^p+b|=r^p>0$, and every value is strictly greater than $r^p$. Moreover $|pb|=0<r^p$, proving the assertion in this case.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, inseparable immediate case, printed p. 39; the prime-degree purely inseparable reduction is written by differentiating the minimal polynomial.

proof.text: Now suppose $f$ is separable. Put $r=r_\alpha$. Apply the coefficient-normalization lemma, whose hypotheses are precisely completeness of $A$, immediacy and degree $p$, separability, and the positive unattained distance established above. Replace $\alpha$ by $\beta=\alpha-c_0$ and write its minimal polynomial as $$F(T)=T^p+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}u_iT^i+b.$$ Translation does not change the infimum $r$. With $R=|\beta|>r$, the lemma gives $|u_1|\le r^{p-1}$, $|u_i|R^i<r^p$ for $2\le i<p$, and $|p|R^p<r^p$. The evaluation formula from step 3 gives $|b|=R^p$ and $|F(c)|=|\beta-c|^p$. Set $a=-u_1$, $g(T)=T^p-aT+b$, and $s=r^p$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, separable immediate case, printed p. 40, coefficient estimates and the instruction to remove the terms of degrees 2 through p-1.

proof.text: For $|c|\le R$, the finite sum $H(c)=F(c)-g(c)=\sum_{i=2}^{p-1}u_ic^i$ has norm $<s$, while $|F(c)|=|\beta-c|^p>s$. The ultrametric inequality applied in both directions gives $|g(c)|=|F(c)|>s$. If $|c|>R$, then $|b|=R^p<|c|^p$ and $|ac|\le r^{p-1}|c|<|c|^p$; hence the leading term strictly dominates and $|g(c)|=|c|^p>s$. The empty sum for $p=2$ is zero and satisfies the same estimate.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40, deletion of intermediate terms; explicit estimate on the ball of radius R and on its complement.

proof.text: Take $c_n\in A$ with $|\beta-c_n|\to r$. Since $r<R$, eventually $|\beta-c_n|<R$, whence $|c_n|=R$ by the ultrametric inequality. Step 6 gives $|g(c_n)|=|\beta-c_n|^p\to r^p=s$. Together with the strict lower bound for every $c$, this proves $s=\inf_c|g(c)|>0$ and nonattainment. Finally $|pb|=|p|R^p<s$ by the normalization estimate. These are all the required clauses.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, printed p. 40, conclusion of (i): the infimum and its nonattainment and the inequality for pb.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.1.4, immediate cases, printed pp. 39–40, read online because the cited local PDF is missing. The assembly replaces the Berkovich-disc/root/Krasner end of the proof with the constant-term norm formula and an explicit two-region estimate.

The local PDF is missing; I fetched the author's PDF from the node URL and saved a copy at src_dl/temkin.pdf. The item statement is unchanged and is the a,b part of 6.1.1. Step 1 (degree p via degree multiplicativity and the minimal-polynomial kernel) is correct. Step 2 (r>0 by completeness; r not attained via equal value groups and residue fields) is correct and elementary. Step 3 (|f(c)|=|alpha-c|^p from the constant-term leaf applied to f(T+c)) is correct. Step 4 (an inseparable irreducible f has f'=0, so char p and f=T^p+b, a=0, |pb|=0) is correct and matches Temkin p.39. Step 5 checks every hypothesis of the normalization node. Step 6 checks both regions: for |c|<=R the error H stays below s<|F(c)|; for |c|>R the leading term c^p dominates; p=2 has H=0. Step 7 gets the exact infimum from an approximating sequence and gives |pb|=p. Tested p=2, Artin-Schreier, and the discrete case (vacuous). It does not restate the item.
